subject: Clarify token billing math: context tokens, rounding, and minimums
messages:
From: Claudia Vega <claudia@brightwave.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightwave.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Question on token math for our expected workload

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to confirm a few specifics from a billing standpoint before we move to the SOW:

1) When you say "tokens billed include prompt + completion," can you confirm whether context retained via KV cache (session continuation) is billed on every inference call or only when new tokens are generated? In our pipeline we re-use long context windows across a batch of 5 requests; curious how that shows up in billing.

2) Do you round token usage per request? For example, if a single API call consumes 1,432 tokens, is that billed as 1,432 tokens, or rounded up to a breakpoint (e.g., next 100)?

3) Are there any per-request minimums or monthly minimums that would affect our committed discount tier? We plan to commit to a 3.5M token/month baseline for the first quarter.

Could you send a short worked example (we have an internal spreadsheet, but a vendor example is helpful for procurement)?

Appreciate it — Claudia
Claudia Vega
Head of Data Products | Brightwave Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Claudia Vega <claudia@brightwave.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on token math for our expected workload

Claudia — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together the short answers below and attached a one-sheet example. High-level: we bill for all tokens processed by the model (prompt + completion), and we have different rounding/packaging behavior for Hosted vs Dedicated customers; I'll summarize both and call out the relevant piece for your procurement ask.

1) KV cache / session continuation: billed tokens include the tokens actually sent to the model on each request. If your client re-sends the full context on each call, those tokens count each time. If you use our session tokenization + KV cache where only the delta is sent (and the server-side KV is referenced), only the new tokens are billed for that specific request. In short: billing correlates to tokens transmitted to the runtime at inference time, not the logical conversation history stored in your app.

2) Rounding: for Hosted API customers we bill at 1-token granularity (no per-request rounding), so 1,432 tokens is billed as 1,432 tokens. For Dedicated customers on reserved capacity we offer an alternate billing unit ("billing units") for committed contracts which maps to 1,000-token buckets for pricing simplicity; those are applied at the invoice level (we consume your committed units first, then overage is per-token).

3) Minimums & discounts: the committed discount tiers apply to usage consumed against the reserved capacity commitment. For a month-to-month Hosted plan there is no per-request minimum; discounts are applied as a percent off list rate by tier once monthly usage crosses thresholds. For your proposed 3.5M token/month commit, that lands you in our "Standard Commitment" bracket (maps to 12% off list for the token profile you showed). If you sign a 12-month Dedicated commit we can extend to 18% and move you to the billing-unit bucket pricing referenced above.

Attached: usage_example_calcs.xlsx (worked scenarios showing a mix of repeated context and short chats).

Let me know if you'd like a one-page SOW + pricing exhibit; Marissa will include that in the next doc.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on token math for our expected workload

Claudia — looping in Kar that handles billing mechanics and invoicing so we can be explicit in the SOW pricing exhibit. A couple of clarifications on our side that will affect the worked example:

- Are you planning to use our session KV feature with server-side KV (so the client sends only deltas)? If yes, please confirm the average delta size and frequency (we can use the sample you shared in the spreadsheet).
- For the 3.5M committed tokens, do you want the commitment to be applied to Hosted (consumption-backed) or Dedicated (reserved capacity) style? Procurement often prefers committed monthly spend on Dedicated for predictability.

Karthik — for Brightwave I've flagged two pricing paths in the spreadsheet: (A) Hosted with volume discounts applied monthly (no rounding), and (B) Dedicated 12-month commit using 1k-token billing units with an 18% discount and an overage rate per-token. Please confirm if we can offer a one-time onboarding credit of $6,000 tied to the 12-month commit (that is our standard play for deals at this size) — I'll note it in the SOW draft.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks — that's super helpful and lines up with our needs. A few quick follow-ups:

- We'll use server-side KV for the majority of sessions (approx. 70% of calls will be deltas of ~80 tokens; 30% will be full context rehydrations averaging ~1,200 tokens). I've updated the spreadsheet tab "BW assumptions" with those numbers.
- Brightwave prefers the predictability of a Dedicated 12-month commit if the economics below hold: 18% discount, 1k-token billing units for commitment accounting, and the $6k onboarding credit.
- Procurement requests the SOW + pricing exhibit in DocuSign for signatures; can you send the SOW_Brightwave_v2.pdf and the DocuSign link?

If you confirm the dedicated terms we'll route this to legal and procurement next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Claudia

Head of Data Products | Brightwave Analytics
